claim_text: The live canonical Hermes config's fallback_providers chain is, in order: opencode-go/glm-5.3-flash, opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash, nvidia/deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash, openai-codex/gpt-6-luna (4 entries, config.yaml:227-235).
The live canonical Hermes primary is model.default=minimax-m3.1-flash-free, provider=opencode-go, base_url=https://opencode.ai/zen/go, api_mode=anthropic_messages (config.yaml:8-13).
Both candidate ids exist in the provider's own live model list for the Go subscription: minimax-m3.1-flash-free and mimo-v2.6-flash (37 ids returned).

minimax-m3.1-flash-free serves a real completion over /v1/chat/completions (HTTP 200, served model minimax-m3.1-flash-free, content MM31F_PROBE_OK) and over /v1/messages with x-api-key (HTTP 200, MM_ANTHROPIC_OK).
mimo-v2.6-flash serves a real completion over /v1/chat/completions (HTTP 200, served model mimo-v2.6-flash, content MIMO26F_PROBE_OK).
Both candidate arms serve through the Hermes client itself: hermes_cli/main.py -m <model> --provider opencode-go -z returned exit 0 with HERMES_MINIMAX_PROBE_OK and HERMES_MIMO_PROBE_OK.

Hermes derives the fallback arm's api_mode per model for the opencode-go family: minimax-* -> anthropic_messages; mimo-*, glm-*, deepseek-* -> chat_completions (hermes_cli/models.py:2331-2348 _OPENCODE_API_MODE_PREFIXES).

Because the chain entry carries no base_url key, the anthropic_messages base (no /v1) is the one the runtime will use for the minimax arm; the opencode-go provider requires the x-opencode-session header on completion endpoints (HTTP 400 MissingSessionID without it) and the anthropic wire requires x-api-key (Authorization: Bearer yields 'Go requires a credential').

RESIDUAL: with the live primary being minimax-m3.1-flash-free on opencode-go, a chain entry {provider: opencode-go, model: minimax-m3.1-flash-free} is SKIPPED by _should_skip_fallback_candidate -> should_skip_candidate(..., FailureScope.MODEL) -> same_deployment, because same_deployment returns True when providers match and models match and the base_url comparison cannot separate them (candidate base_url is empty). Measured: skipped=True for that entry; skipped=False for mimo-v2.6-flash, glm-5.3-flash, deepseek-v4.1-flash, nvidia/... and gpt-6-luna.

Consequence of C9: after the owner-ordered re-order, the effective first SERVABLE fallback while the primary remains MiniMax is mimo-v2.6-flash, not minimax-m3.1-flash-free. The chain order is still exactly as ordered; the skip is a runtime guard against re-selecting the backend that just failed.

The HGK registry's declared PLAN lane chain (registry routes[].PLAN.arms/fallbacks, assignment lane_chains.PLAN, pool PLAN ordered_pool ranks 2-3, AGENTS.md line 53) names opencode-go/glm-5.3-flash as its fallback1 and opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash as its fallback2 — i.e. the first TWO entries of the live Hermes chain, in the same order, but only 2 of the live 4.

The HGK registry explicitly records the live Hermes config as NON_AUTHORITATIVE for governed HGK calls: 'Its delegation and global fallback_providers are NON_AUTHORITATIVE for governed HGK calls. Recorded as observation; drift here is never a hard failure.' (registry:501). The registry's projections[] do not bind the live config's fallback_providers, so changing the live chain does NOT trip the drift gate.

The registry's declared lane chains are the LANE-DISPATCH declaration (Codex CLI lanes EXECUTE / VERIFY_SECURITY); the in-Hermes PLAN & Orchestrator plane is a separate binding surface (profiles/hgk-governed/config.yaml model.default=gpt-6.1-sol / openai-codex). Re-binding the registry's PLAN lane chain is therefore a LANE-CHAIN REBIND, a different control-plane act from the main-model fallback chain re-order.

The lane dispatcher's own selection chain for the in-Hermes PLAN lane is the governed profile binding, NOT the live canonical config's fallback_providers; the canonical config's fallback chain governs the main agent and ordinary delegation children.

A registry conformance test pins the owner chain: tests/test_lane_policy.py:104-105 asserts PLAN == [(openai-codex, gpt-6.1-sol), (opencode-go, glm-5.3-flash), (opencode-go, deepseek-v4.1-flash)] and the same for VERIFY_SECURITY. Re-binding the registry's PLAN chain would require changing this test in the same change set.

The live canonical Hermes config is actively rewritten by another actor during the session (observed digests ad4ee7e4... at 12:10:08, c9308966... at 12:32:39), so any apply must carry a full-digest pre-image guard and re-verify immediately before writing.

Both candidate arms resolve a context window without error (minimax-m3.1-flash-free -> 1,000,000; mimo-v2.6-flash -> 1,048,576) so the fallback switch does not trip the compressor's context-length re-derivation.

No actual failover EVENT was observed: no live log line shows the chain activating. What is proven is the chain's configuration, each arm's servability, the runtime's arm-resolution and skip mechanics — not an observed failover.

Static provider-catalog metadata for minimax-m3.1-flash-free and mimo-v2.6-flash could not be confirmed by import (PROVIDER_MODELS is not the exported name in hermes_cli/models_catalog_static.py); the live catalog lists minimax-m3 / minimax-m2.7 / minimax-m2.5 but NOT minimax-m3.1-flash-free, and lists mimo-v2.5 / mimo-v2.5-pro / mimo-v2-pro / mimo-v2-omni but NOT mimo-v2.6-flash. The ids therefore route but are absent from the curated static catalog.
